title: Runtime Policy Reconciler for Per-Tenant Canary Coordination
creator: Aisha Malik
description:
Goal: Build a runtime-side reconciliation service that translates and enforces high-level canary/A-B/shadow policies into environment-specific deployment plans for Hosted, Dedicated, and Private modes. The reconciler will detect configuration drift, perform preflight compatibility simulation, synthesize safe traffic schedules per-tenant, and emit machine-readable plans for the rollout controller to execute.

Why: Customers run across heterogeneous environments with different constraints (network egress limits, KMS/HSM availability, quantization/FP support, autoscaling granularity). A single canary configuration declared by a product team should be reconciled into concrete, enforceable actions per environment instead of relying on manual translation by SREs. This reduces rollouts failing due to environment mismatches and enables consistent safety guarantees regardless of deployment mode.

Scope: PoC for per-tenant policy reconciliation, simulator for compatibility checks, translation plug-in interface (for mapping features that differ across environments), telemetry hooks for auditing and automated rollback triggers. Excludes in-depth integration with billing/quotas in this iteration (follow-up work).
acceptance_criteria: Reconciler can ingest a single high-level canary spec and produce 3 environment-specific rollout plans (Hosted, Dedicated, Private) that the rollout executor can apply without additional manual changes.
Preflight simulator flags incompatible features (e.g., KV-cache hot-warm placement, HSM-only key rotations) and indicates suggested fallbacks in the plan.
Automated safety checks improve: at least one detected drift gets prevented in canary trials during validation runs in staging.
Telemetry emitted for each synthesized plan that includes decision rationale and a linkable audit id for console display.
Auto-rollback hooks are wired: executor will trigger rollback if error-rate > 2% OR p95 latency increases by >30% versus baseline OR quality regression on a seeded eval set exceeds threshold.

comments: 2026-02-26 — Aisha Malik: Kickoff notes uploaded to Confluence (link below). Identified top 5 incompatibilities between Hosted/Dedicated/Private from spike: HSM availability, explicit egress rules, GPU model flavor/quantization mismatch, autoscaler granularity, network latency assumptions.

2026-03-03 — Evelyn Chen: Spike complete. Added compatibility matrix and sample translation recipes for common cases (quantization fallback -> use int8 runtime path with KV cache eviction heuristics).

2026-03-08 — Jonah Park: Implemented initial adapter scaffold. Early tests show that Private clusters without HSM require plan adjustment to avoid KMS key rotation steps. Decided to implement plugin warning + auto-fallback rather than blocking rollout in this iteration.

2026-03-11 — Marco Alvarez: Preflight simulator prototype can replay 10k synthetic requests against Dedicated staging and report p95 delta and error spikes. Need to expand to include seeded eval set for quality checks.

2026-03-14 — Aisha Malik: Product review: PM likes the audit_id visibility requirement; asked that reconciler annotate which tenants require manual approval due to regulatory constraints (e.g., no cross-region fallbacks). Added to acceptance criteria.
notes: Trade-offs: We prefer best-effort auto-fallbacks for most incompatibilities to allow automated rollouts, but will gate critical regulatory mismatches behind manual approval. This keeps velocity for non-sensitive tenants while protecting high-risk customers.

Perf risk: Preflight simulations are approximate — production behavior may differ under real traffic patterns. The reconciler will therefore schedule conservative initial exposure (e.g., 1% -> 5% increments) and rely on short evaluation windows before ramping.
Operational: Audit events must be searchable in Console with links back to the exact synthesized plan. Plan immutability after creation reduces confusion during rollbacks.
Future: Follow-up work should add quota-aware cost estimation and integration with Dedicated capacity reservations so the reconciler can propose reservations when needed.
release_notes: PoC release: runtime-1.21: reconciler service + adapter interface + preflight simulator. Console shows reconciliation rationale for staging runs.
Known limitations: Does not yet synthesize explicit billing/reservation requests for Dedicated; manual approval required for tenants with regulatory flags.
